title: The Regiment of Nagasaki's harbor
premise: In 1860s Nagasaki's foreign settlement, Juniper Brightwater, daughter of an English typeface cutter, has passed as her father's son 'Jun' for years to keep the family print shop invisible to authorities. When a census taker notices the discrepancy, he offers silence in exchange for a favor: deliver a sealed letter to Katsuo Mori, a Japanese printer now branded an enemy collaborator. Juniper's promise made in peacetime pulls her into the underground network of dissident printers, forcing her to choose between the identity that keeps her safe and the justice she can no longer ignore. The novel ends with Juniper publicly reclaiming her name at her father's press, printing the truth that condemns the census taker's masters even as it exposes her own.
about_author: Marguerite Halloran is the pen name of a former letterpress restorer who spent a decade cataloguing Meiji-era printing houses in Kyushu. She writes historical fiction about people whose names were deliberately left out of official records.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. During the annual census of the harbor district, an official named Endo lingers over the Brightwater entry, asking why 'Jun' never appears in church registers. Juniper deflects, but that night she burns old letters and realizes her invisibility is fraying. Emotional beat: dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: Lead and Memory
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Flashback woven through present work: how her dying father taught her to cut type and made her swear to keep the shop running under his name. She sorts his punches by hand, grieving. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden and love.

chapters.title: Endo's Price
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Endo returns privately, revealing he knows she is a woman. He will stay silent if she delivers a sealed letter to Katsuo Mori, a Japanese printer declared an enemy collaborator, before the month's end. Emotional beat: coercion dressed as courtesy.

chapters.title: The Harbor at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. She crosses the harbor's back channels to find Mori's shuttered workshop, where she meets his sister Hana, who guards the door with a boat hook. The letter is not delivered; Hana demands to know who sent it. Emotional beat: suspicion between strangers.

chapters.title: What Was Promised in Peacetime
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Inside the workshop, Juniper discovers the letter contains half a printing plate her father hid there years ago—the plate for a banned broadsheet documenting a massacre the government denies. Her father had promised to help print it when peace allowed. Emotional beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: The Regiment Assembles
chapters.summary: POV alternating Juniper and Hana. Dissident printers gather secretly in the shop's cellar: typesetters, a defected soldier, a widow who smuggles paper. They call themselves a regiment without uniforms. Juniper must decide whether to lend her father's press. Emotional beat: cautious solidarity.

chapters.title: A Name Cut in Reverse
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Printing by night, Juniper teaches Hana typecutting; Hana teaches her the harbor's escape routes. Endo grows impatient, hinting he wants the plate destroyed, not delivered. Juniper suspects whose side he truly serves. Emotional beat: intimacy and mounting paranoia.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: POV Hana. Soldiers raid the waterfront following a tip. The regiment scatters; the press is seized, and Juniper is arrested under her father's name—a man who cannot exist. In custody, her double life collapses entirely. Emotional beat: exposure as catastrophe and strange relief.

chapters.title: Testimony in Type
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Facing charges of fraud and sedition, Juniper bargains with Endo's superior: she will surrender quietly if the confiscated broadsheet is read aloud into the trial record. The massacre enters the official transcript, unerasable. Emotional beat: justice seized from the law's own machinery.

chapters.title: Juniper Brightwater, Printer
chapters.summary: POV Juniper. Months later, released under amnesty, Juniper reopens the shop under her own full name, with Hana as partner. The first job off the new press is the completed broadsheet, freely sold. History no longer happens to other people. Emotional beat: identity claimed, inheritance fulfilled.
